consequence: Lead-time reliability has no effect on any buffer. Two suppliers with identical demand dispersion get the identical safety stock whether their lead time is metronomic or swings by nine days, and on this network that is not a hypothetical: 16,198 of 17,829 published supplier-period rows carry a non-zero lead-time standard deviation, mean OTD is 15.08%, and lead times run from 5 to 31 days. The second consequence is a screen: the reference's Safety Stock page decomposes a buffer into demand variability and lead-time variability, and that decomposition cannot be published at all, because one of its two drivers does not exist in the implementation. It was withheld on those grounds rather than filled with a term that would have been the whole buffer relabelled.

evidence.declaredFormula: contracts/guardrails/inventory-policy-v2.yaml:174 safetyStock.formula = service_level_z * sqrt(protection_weeks * demand_variance_weekly + mean_weekly_demand^2 * lead_time_variance_weeks). Two addends.
evidence.firstAddendIsReconciled: The demand term is computed from the accepted forecast interval rather than from a demand_variance_weekly estimate, and that substitution is declared: safetyStock.intervalSource = accepted_forecast_p90_minus_p50, with the division by the 0.90 normal quantile converting a P90 spread into a one-sigma equivalent. The formula TEXT is stale about it; the code is not wrong. This is called out separately so the real gap is not lost inside a wording complaint.
evidence.implementedExpression: ml/src/retail_ml/engines/primitives.py:180 returns service_level_z(service_level) * fractional_horizon_rss(weekly_spreads, protection_days) / NormalDist().inv_cdf(0.90). One term. There is no lead_time_variance_weeks anywhere in the engine.

policyKeysWithNoConsumer.leadTime.minimumObservations: Declared 8. Ten suppliers publish fewer than eight periods (3 with one, 1 with two, 3 with three, 3 with five), so the threshold has a real population and nothing applies it.
policyKeysWithNoConsumer.leadTime.variabilityMethod: Declared supplier_performance_mean_and_std. The std half has no reader.
policyKeysWithNoConsumer.leadTime.zeroVarianceBehavior: Declared reason_code_not_zero_buffer, with zeroVarianceReasonCode LEAD_TIME_VARIABILITY_UNAVAILABLE. 1,631 rows do publish a zero standard deviation, so the reason code has a real population and can never be emitted -- there is no code path that could emit it.

evidence.secondAddendIsAbsent: Lead time enters the engine only through protection_days -- leadTime.protectionPeriodFormula = lead_time_days + review_period_days -- which sizes the RSS window. That consumes the MEAN. The variance is never read.
evidence.theInputExistsAndIsPublished: canonical_data.supplier_performance.lead_time_std_days over run-adac9e85dccb56e8: 17,829 rows across 279 suppliers, min 0.000, median 1.286, max 9.500, non-zero on 16,198 rows. The datum the formula needs is canonical, declared in retail_v2/schema.yaml and reaches the ML tier already.

fix.guardrail: Whatever is published must let the two drivers be told apart, or the Safety Stock decomposition stays withheld. Publishing a single number under two driver labels would be worse than the current withholding.
fix.openQuestion: Whether the frozen policy's formula is the target, or whether the interval-only buffer is the intended design and the policy text plus its four orphaned leadTime keys should be corrected to say so. That is a policy decision, not an implementation one, which is why this record proposes no default. Note that P4-D13 forbids weakening a threshold after seeing a result, so the choice should be made on the design and not on which buffer the demo prefers.

measuredOn: run-adac9e85dccb56e8 curated publication; engine expression read from ml/src/retail_ml/engines/primitives.py

resolution.change: safety_stock_units now returns a SafetyStock carrying total_units, demand_units, lead_time_units and lead_time_reason_code, and adds mean_weekly_demand^2 * lead_time_variance_weeks under the same root. The demand term is untouched -- a test pins that, because implementing the second addend by rewriting the first would move every previously published buffer for a reason nobody chose. Variance comes from supplier_performance.lead_time_std_days as leadTime.variabilityMethod declares, squared over weeks.
resolution.decision: The declared formula is authoritative. The contract states two addends and its leadTime block declares the sourcing, threshold and reason code for the second, which nobody writes intending an interval-only buffer. P4-D13 was initially cited as blocking this and that was wrong: D13 forbids weakening a threshold after seeing a result, not implementing a declared formula. What it forbids is reverting this because a gate moved.

policyKeysNowConsumed.leadTime.minimumObservations: Enforced. The loader now carries observation_periods, which the DISTINCT ON previously discarded; 10 of 279 suppliers publish fewer than eight periods and are reason-coded rather than given a one-period standard deviation.
policyKeysNowConsumed.leadTime.variabilityMethod: The std half now has a reader.
policyKeysNowConsumed.leadTime.zeroVarianceBehavior: A zero or absent variance produces a reason, never a zero-variance buffer.
policyKeysNowConsumed.leadTime.zeroVarianceReasonCode: LEAD_TIME_VARIABILITY_UNAVAILABLE was unreachable and now fires on every buffered row -- see theMeasuredEffect.

resolution.published: Migration 0020 adds safety_stock_demand_units, safety_stock_lead_time_units and lead_time_variability_reason_code, with check constraints that each driver is within the total (which quadrature implies and an additive rewrite would violate), that the drivers are paired, and that a reason and a non-zero contribution are mutually exclusive. The interval gate obliges both drivers with the total; the reason code is deliberately not obliged, since null is the healthy case.
resolution.tests: 8 new engine tests including quadrature, the untouched demand term, a more erratic supplier getting a larger buffer, and reason-coding rather than zero-variance. ml 343 passed.

theMeasuredEffect.headline: The addend is implemented and correct, and changes no number in THIS network. That is a data-shape fact, not an implementation gap, and it is the most important thing in this record.
theMeasuredEffect.predictionThatDidNotHappen: Buffers were expected to rise and possibly flip meanInventoryUnits. They did not move, so the replay gates are byte-identical to the previous run (india-west holdout still 52 vs 25 stockout periods, 2,729 vs 71 lost units). Reported because it was predicted, not quietly dropped.
theMeasuredEffect.result: All 963 buffered rows are stores, all 963 carry LEAD_TIME_VARIABILITY_UNAVAILABLE, the lead-time driver sums to 0 and the demand driver sums to 14,217.31 -- equal to the total, as it must be.
theMeasuredEffect.whatWouldMakeItFire: A node-level forecast for a DC, or a store supplied directly by an external supplier. Either makes the term compute with no further code change.
theMeasuredEffect.why: A cell has a buffer only if it has a forecast interval, and only stores do: 2,188 DC cells are assessed and 0 are buffered, because a DC has no node-level forecast (NODE_INTERVAL_BASIS_UNAVAILABLE). A cell has measurable lead-time variability only if an external supplier serves it, and only DCs are externally supplied -- a store is replenished over an internal service lane whose origin is our own DC, which publishes no supplier performance. The two conditions never co-occur.

resolution.verified: ir_1a51973dd1a17d32 activated and serving. Row level: safety_stock 771.6268 = demand 771.6268, lead 0, reason LEAD_TIME_VARIABILITY_UNAVAILABLE. Summary: demand 14,217.31, lead 0, leadTimeVariabilityWithheldCells 963 of 963 assessed.
resolution.whyItIsStillWorthHaving: Three things changed even though no buffer did. The reason code now fires and states the truth instead of the engine silently omitting a declared term. The Safety Stock driver decomposition has a source and is published rather than withheld -- it correctly shows the demand driver carrying the whole buffer and says why the other is zero. And the formula is in place for the moment the data shape changes, rather than being discovered missing then.

rootCause: Contract and implementation diverge, and the same class as FORECAST_HEALTH_GRAIN_MISMATCH: the contract states the semantics and nothing enforces them. Policy v2 declares a two-addend buffer plus the apparatus for sourcing, thresholding and reason-coding lead-time variability; the engine implements the demand addend and no part of the lead-time one.
summary: Policy v2's safetyStock.formula declares a lead-time-variance addend, and its leadTime block declares where that input comes from, how many observations it needs and what reason code stands in when it is zero. The engine implements none of it: lead time reaches the buffer only as a mean that sizes the protection window, so four policy keys and one reason code have no consumer and a supplier's unreliability changes no buffer.
